conventions.convention: The central-potential model is spinless on L²(R³; C), with inner product linear in the first argument. Its baseline potential is real, bounded and measurable, V(x)=v(|x|) for x≠0, with V(0)=0; its energy domain is W²,²(R³; C).
The Fourier transform uses exp(−2πix·ξ); the physical free-energy multiplier is (2π²ℏ²/m)|ξ|², giving −ℏ²Δw/(2m) on the full Sobolev domain.

Spherical reduction here uses u∈C_c∞((0,∞)); the radial/operator equivalence is almost everywhere for measurable v and pointwise when v is continuous. Only nonzero vectors define preparations, after normalization.

For the attractive one-centre model, ℏ,m,κ>0, γ=2mκ/ℏ², Hκ=(ℏ²/2m)Cγ on H²(R³; C), aκ=ℏ²/(mκ). Radial domains are transported from the three-dimensional operator through the closed-form realization, rather than chosen by a formal boundary condition.
The two particles are distinguishable and spinless; charges are −q₋,+q₊, κ=q₋q₊/(4πε₀), R=(m₁x₁+m₂x₂)/(m₁+m₂), r=x₁−x₂, and μ=m₁m₂/(m₁+m₂). The neutral branch has q₋=q₊=q; hydrogen has Z=1 and q=e.
Principal labels start at n=1, with 0≤l≤n−1 and −l≤m≤l. The n² degeneracy is spatial and spinless; completeness concerns the negative spectral subspace, not all L².

Reduced functions use measure dr, with ψ=u(r)Ylm(Ω)/r and normalized angular harmonics. The examples choose unit radial norm and positive real Laguerre coefficient; their cross-l overlap therefore has the specified sign.

All physical conclusions are conditional model deductions. No spectroscopy experiment or numerical parameter evaluation is reported; laboratory identification and measured inputs require separate preparation, calibration, sampling and uncertainty records.

load_bearing.statement: The assigned one-centre energy operator is Hκ=(ℏ²/2m)Cγ, γ=2mκ/ℏ², with domain H²(R³; C). The declared two-body operator on H²(R⁶; C) has the centre-of-mass/relative reading with reduced mass μ=m₁m₂/(m₁+m₂).

The eigenvalues of Hκ are exactly En=−mκ²/(2ℏ²n²), n≥1; the eigenspace at En has dimension n² and is spanned by the stated normalized bound vectors. Those vectors form a complete orthonormal family of the negative spectral subspace; the nonnegative spectral subspace is infinite dimensional and contains no eigenvectors.

Hκ is self-adjoint and bounded below on H², has essential spectrum [0,∞), and generates U(t)=exp(−itHκ/ℏ). The norm-differentiable Schrödinger equation holds exactly for initial vectors in its domain, and stationary pure preparations are exactly its eigenrays.

UΦH₂UΦ⁻¹=T_R⊗I+I⊗Cμ. The relative levels are −μκ²/(2ℏ²n²), whereas σ(H₂)=[−μκ²/(2ℏ²),∞) and H₂ has no eigenvalues. Each relative level is the lower endpoint of its continuous centre-of-mass channel. The lifted total-momentum components have no nonzero L² eigenvectors.

For each labeled bound vector ψnlm=u_nlYlm/r, its normalized position law disintegrates into |u_nl|²/∥u_nl∥² times the angular weight. The ground radial density is 4r²aκ⁻³exp(−2r/aκ), with mean 3aκ/2 and unique mode aκ.
D(H₀)=W²,²(R³; C) and H₀f=−ℏ²Δwf/(2m) for every f in that domain. Adding any real bounded measurable V gives the same weak differential operator on the same domain.
Assume Countable Choice. For every real λ>0 and integer k≥0, ∫₀∞rᵏexp(−λr)dr=k!/λᵏ⁺¹.

concerns.concern: Definition (e) says “the value 0 is called the continuum threshold of the model”, although (b) permits every real bounded measurable central potential without an asymptotic-zero hypothesis. For the admissible constant v(r)=V₀>0, HV=Hfree+V₀I has spectrum and continuum beginning at V₀, not zero. The wording needs to distinguish a declared energy reference from a spectral threshold, or justify a restricted threshold claim.

The physical_scope claims the position law “of any normalised bound state” disintegrates into “the radial density |u_nl|²/||u_nl||² times the angular spherical-harmonic weight”. The Statement and proof establish this for each labeled separated vector Ψnlm. A normalized eigenvector such as (Ψ200+Ψ210)/√2 is also a bound state under the model definition, but its position density has angular-radial cross terms and its radial marginal is (p20+p21)/2, not a single labeled p_nl. The public scope is stronger than the proved claim.

The Statement fixes the mass parameter m>0 and then quantifies the angular label with the same symbol in “−l≤m≤l”, while retaining m in En=−mκ²/(2ℏ²n²). These distinct quantities need distinct notation; the spherical-reduction item already uses a barred magnetic label. The intended energy and degeneracy calculation is clear.

Fact F2 attributes “square integrable exactly in this terminating case” to thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination (c),(d). That supplier proves termination iff the series is polynomial and proves L² integrability in the terminating case; nonintegrability in the nonterminating case is supplied separately by thm-nrqm-coulomb-laguerre-bound-energy-exhaustion (a). The earlier bound-spectrum theorem provides sufficient context, but this particular citation overstates its named supplier.

alerts.finding: The citing page qm-light-matter-and-spectral-transitions-examples summarizes this item as computing “1/√3” for both the entries ⟨Y10,Q0Y00⟩ and ⟨Y1,±1,Q±Y00⟩. The item's Example (b) and Verification 2.1 instead give ⟨Y1,±1,Q±Y00⟩=∓1/√3 under its explicitly fixed spherical-harmonic phases. The page's positive value is correct for their modulus, but not for both signed entries as written. This finding concerns the citing page summary; the item's signed calculation is correct.

seams_checked.note: No entanglement or reduced-state theorem is restated as a central-potential premise. The two-body composition uses P1 and the explicit mathematical tensor/product suppliers.

Operator domains, endpoint realization, spectral exhaustion, degeneracy and two-body decomposition are faithfully transported. However, the radial-distribution item's F2 attributes the nontermination L² converse to the Kummer supplier, which does not state that converse; see concern.
The positive-scaling lemma is used with a positive scalar and unchanged domain. No one-dimensional boundary realization is imported into the three-dimensional Coulomb domain.
The free multiplier convention, W²,² domain, bounded-potential restriction, Hilbert tensor construction and Euclidean L² product unitary match the supplier statements.
P1, P2, P4–P7 remain adopted assumptions. SI dimensions and the empirical status of permeability, species parameters and laboratory identification are retained.
The s=0 specialization preserves the maximal position/momentum domains and normalized Born position law. Singular Coulomb energy is introduced separately from P5's bounded-potential baseline.
Sharp observables retain their self-adjoint domains and declared units; scalar laws, spectral support and eigenspace atom weights are used as stated, without a joint-measurement claim.
Density preparations and pure rays are used with zero excluded. Unnormalized spherical vectors are normalized before a Born preparation law is asserted.
Flow sign is exp(−itH/ℏ); norm differentiability retains the energy-domain hypothesis, and the stationary-pure-state iff eigenray criterion is preserved.
Normalized spherical harmonics and their complete angular family are used with polar surface measure. No spin multiplicity is added to the spatial n² degeneracy.
Energy, length, action and charge dimensions are consistent. α=κ/(ℏc) is dimensionless; no numerical measured input is introduced.
Radial probabilities are normalized pushforwards of the s=0 position law, rather than trajectories or measured radii.
The Laguerre template is specialized to n≤2 with explicit positive phases. Normalizations, moments and the cross-l overlap −√3/2 follow from the displayed integrals.
The static finite-level dipole postulate selects the equal-charge neutral branch and the relative-coordinate factor with mass μ; it does not treat a relative bound vector as a total H₂ eigenvector.
The Stark example uses a declared two-state compression of the relative Coulomb operator at mass μ, with the correct E1, E2, gap and radial moment supplier.

The Coulomb adiabatic item uses the exact common H² domain and the n²-dimensional isolated level along a positive C² coupling path. Time dependence is an additional protocol, not attributed to autonomous P4.
Free weak-Laplacian identification and Coulomb self-adjointness/flow are used on their exact domains. The Dollard model keeps Coulomb separate from the short-range classes.
Dipole selection rules consume the relative charged-pair model and labeled Coulomb bound vectors. Field coupling, finite-level compression and emission assumptions are additional model data.

The example uses the labeled bound-state family for angular factors and makes no claim that these factors establish a transition probability or measured spectrum. Its citing page has the signed-factor summary defect recorded in alerts.
